answers.explanation: Catabolism is the breakdown of complex substances into simpler ones, releasing energy.
The eyespot is the light-sensitive organ of Euglena, which helps it move towards light.
Mitochondria release energy by respiration and chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis, so both are needed in active cells.
Taenia solium, the pork tapeworm, has its cysts in pigs.
Structure II is the clitellum, the swollen glandular band of the earthworm that produces the cocoon.
Earthworms live in soils rich in humus, which is the decomposed organic matter they feed on.
Arthropods have a body covered by an exoskeleton made of chitin.
Moths have a fatter abdomen than butterflies, which is one of the features that distinguishes them.
Quill feathers, the long primary and secondary feathers of the wing, are used for flight.
Xerophytes are plants adapted to grow in deserts and very dry areas.
A virus is the simplest form of life, with only genetic material and a protein coat, and no cell structure.
A proboscis is a sucking mouthpart found in insects such as butterflies and moths.
Spiny leaves reduce water loss by transpiration, which is a structural adaptation of desert plants.
Long, sharp clawed feet are used by birds of prey for grasping their prey.
Anabaena is a photosynthetic blue-green alga that uses energy from the sun to make food.
Translocation is the movement of minerals and manufactured food within the plant.
Ptyalin is the enzyme present in saliva that begins the digestion of starch.
Carnivorous plants have special devices for trapping and digesting insects.
Respiration transforms the chemical energy in cellular fuels into the high energy bonds of ATP.
Fungi lack chlorophyll, so they cannot make their own food and must obtain it from other organisms, which makes them heterotrophs.
Plasmodium is a parasitic protozoan that causes malaria.
Lymphocytes are white blood cells that produce antibodies and take part in the immune response of vertebrates.
The vertebrate circulatory system consists of the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins.
Xylem is the plant tissue that carries water and mineral salts from the roots.
Platelets help blood to clot by forming a plug at the site of injury.
Plasma makes up about 55 percent of the volume of blood.
Sweat glands in the mammalian skin excrete water, salts and urea.
Uric acid is the main nitrogenous waste product of insects.
The skeleton is the main structure in vertebrates that supports and protects the body.
The chitin of the arthropod exoskeleton is strengthened by calcium compounds.
Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma.
The stamen is the male reproductive organ of a flower, producing pollen in the anther.
The pituitary gland lies just below the hypothalamus and controls many other glands.
Auxin is the most important plant hormone, controlling growth and cell elongation.
Rod cells in the retina are sensitive to dim light.
Antidiuretic hormone controls water reabsorption, so without it the body loses large amounts of water and becomes severely dehydrated.
Oestrogen is synthesised mainly in the ovaries.
A cataract is the clouding of the lens of the eye.
Sewage is biodegradable, since microorganisms break it down, unlike crude oil, heavy metals and cellophane.
Sleeping sickness is caused by Trypanosoma parasites transmitted by tsetse flies.
The lithosphere is the solid part of the earth that makes up the land.
Treponema pallidum is the bacterium that causes syphilis.
People of blood group AB are universal recipients because they have no anti-A or anti-B antibodies.
Agglutination is the clumping together of red blood cells, which occurs in incompatible transfusions.
Aestivation is a physiological response of animals to very dry conditions, in which they become dormant during the dry season.
Cactus opuntia reduces its leaves to spines, which reduces water loss.
A hooked beak and sharp claws are adaptations for feeding on prey in a bird of prey.
Chromatophores are the pigment-containing cells that allow chameleons to change colour.
Social insects live in colonies where individuals depend on one another, which is a form of symbiosis.
